findings.message: No regression test makes a same-value resize push the total over a nonzero maxSize and then evict. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)` with maxSize 10, only reaches the limit exactly. Requirement 3 (evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits, keep the updated entry as most recently used, and dispose evicted entries) is therefore checked by source review only. The source does satisfy it: at src/index.ts:2250, `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (src/index.ts:2303-2304). The `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` loop at src/index.ts:1775-1776 then evicts from the head with eviction disposal, and the updated entry is never evicted because its size was removed and `size <= this.#maxSize`. The spec allows source-review obligations, so this finding does not affect the verdict.

Nothing in the new tests makes a same-value remeasure push the total over maxSize and force LRU eviction. The closest case is `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, which only reaches the limit exactly. The spec makes uncovered clauses source-review obligations, and source review confirms the behaviour. In src/index.ts:2250, `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before src/index.ts:2303-2304 (`this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`). Because of that order, the loop in #addItemSize at src/index.ts:1775-1776 (`while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`) evicts from the head, applies the existing 'evict' dispose/disposeAfter behaviour, and never evicts the updated entry, since its size has already been zeroed and `size <= this.#maxSize`. This is advisory only: the missing regression test is not a demonstrated violation.

Requirement 3 says that when a same-value update grows past the total limit, it must "evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits, retaining the updated entry as most recently used. Each evicted entry must receive the existing eviction disposal behavior." No test in the new file exercises this. The closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })`, brings the total to exactly 10 (`t.equal(c.size, 2)`), so nothing is evicted. A source review shows the behavior is implemented: src/index.ts:2250 `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before src/index.ts:2303-2304 `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`, and #addItemSize evicts from the head with `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`. The spec allows source review for clauses the command does not exercise, so this finding is advisory: a regression test for this path is missing.

None of the new tests covers the eviction clause. A same-value resize that pushes the total over a nonzero maxSize is never tested: the closest case, `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` with `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, lands exactly on the limit and evicts nothing. Eviction disposal and the updated entry staying most-recent therefore rest on source review only. The source looks correct. src/index.ts:2303-2304 calls `this.#removeItemSize(index)` and then `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`. The entry has already been moved to the tail (`this.#moveToTail(index)`, line 2250), and `#addItemSize` runs `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` (lines 1775-1777), which evicts from the head with the existing dispose/disposeAfter behavior. The spec permits source review for this clause, so this is advisory.

None of the new tests trigger LRU eviction from a same-value resize. The closest case is `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, which only reaches the exact limit, so Requirement 3 (evict LRU entries until the total fits, keep the updated entry as most recent, dispose evicted entries) is not covered by the sealed command. Reading the source shows the behaviour is correct: src/index.ts:2250 `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs first, then src/index.ts:2303-2304 `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`, and src/index.ts:1775-1776 `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }` evicts from the head. The updated entry's size is zeroed and it sits at the tail, and the update only runs when `size <= this.#maxSize`, so the updated entry is never evicted. The spec allows source review for clauses the command does not exercise, so this is advisory only.

Requirement 3 (eviction) has no regression test. No test triggers LRU eviction from a same-value remeasure. The closest one is 'validation, entry admission, and exact total limit', which only reaches the exact limit: `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` / `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)` / `t.equal(c.size, 2)`. Reading the source, the behavior looks correct. At src/index.ts:2250 `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs first. Then src/index.ts:2303-2304 call `this.#removeItemSize(index)` and `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)`, and addItemSize runs `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`. That evicts head (LRU) entries using the existing evict disposal, keeps the updated entry at the tail, and disposeAfter is flushed at src/index.ts:2323. The spec says clauses the command does not exercise stay source-review obligations, so this is advisory only.

Nothing in the new test file exercises Requirement 3, which says a same-value resize that pushes the total over a nonzero maxSize "must evict least-recently-used entries until the total fits, retaining the updated entry as most recently used" and that evicted entries receive eviction disposal. The closest test only reaches the exact limit: `c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` followed by `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`, so nothing is evicted. The spec makes unexercised clauses source-review obligations, and source review shows the requirement is met. In src/index.ts:2250, `this.#moveToTail(index)` runs before `this.#removeItemSize(index); this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` at 2303-2304. The eviction loop in #addItemSize at 1775 (`while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`) therefore removes head entries with eviction disposal. It cannot evict the updated entry: its size has already been removed and `size <= this.#maxSize` is guarded at 2301. This is advisory only; a regression test would strengthen it.

None of the new tests covers the eviction requirement: a same-value resize that pushes the total over a nonzero maxSize. The closest case only reaches the exact limit and evicts nothing (`c.set('a', a, { size: 6 })` / `t.equal(c.calculatedSize, 10)`). I checked the source by hand: src/index.ts:2250 calls `this.#moveToTail(index)` before `this.#removeItemSize(index)` / `this.#addItemSize(index, size, status)` (2303-2304). `#addItemSize` loops `while (this.#calculatedSize > maxSize) { this.#evict(true) }`. That `#evict` call fires dispose with reason 'evict' and queues disposeAfter. It cannot evict the updated entry, because that entry's size was zeroed first and the entry now sits at the tail. The requirement looks satisfied, but no test locks it in.

Same-value resizing can leave eviction callbacks undelivered when noDisposeOnSet is true. With maxSize: 10, disposeAfter configured, and entries a(size 3), b(size 4), setting the identical a to size 8 with noDisposeOnSet: true evicts b. src/index.ts:2378 queues "this.#disposed?.push([oldValue, k, 'evict'])", but src/index.ts:2323 guards delivery with "if (!noDisposeOnSet && this.#hasDisposeAfter && this.#disposed)". The successful update therefore returns without calling disposeAfter for b; without another operation, it never runs. The contract requires "Each evicted entry must receive the existing eviction disposal behavior." The public option documentation at src/index.ts:884–886 limits suppression to when "the entry key is still accessible within the cache", which does not apply to evicted b. Drain eviction disposal callbacks even when replacement disposal is suppressed, and cover this interaction in the regression tests.
